Count how many times each word occurs in a sentence, ignoring case and punctuation but keeping apostrophes inside contractions.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/word-count) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: word_count.nomi
import std/regex.Regex

/// How many times each word occurs in `sentence`, lower-cased. A word is a
/// run of letters and digits, and may hold an apostrophe between two of them,
/// as in "can't"; quotes around a word are not part of it.
pub fn count_words(sentence: String) -> Map<String, Int> {
    sentence
    |> String.to_lower()
    |> String.find_all(Regex`[a-z0-9]+('[a-z0-9]+)*`)
    |> Iter.frequencies()
}

// FILE: word_count_test.nomi
import word_count.count_words

test "counts words" {
    cases = [
        #("count one word", "word", %{"word" => 1}),
        #("count one of each word", "one of each", %{"one" => 1, "of" => 1, "each" => 1}),
        #(
            "multiple occurrences of a word",
            "one fish two fish red fish blue fish",
            %{"one" => 1, "fish" => 4, "two" => 1, "red" => 1, "blue" => 1},
        ),
        #("handles cramped lists", "one,two,three", %{"one" => 1, "two" => 1, "three" => 1}),
        #("handles expanded lists", "one,\ntwo,\nthree", %{"one" => 1, "two" => 1, "three" => 1}),
        #(
            "ignore punctuation",
            "car: carpet as java: javascript!!&@$%^&",
            %{"car" => 1, "carpet" => 1, "as" => 1, "java" => 1, "javascript" => 1},
        ),
        #("include numbers", "testing, 1, 2 testing", %{"testing" => 2, "1" => 1, "2" => 1}),
        #("normalize case", "go Go GO Stop stop", %{"go" => 3, "stop" => 2}),
        #(
            "with apostrophes",
            "'First: don't laugh. Then: don't cry. You're getting it.'",
            %{
                "first" => 1,
                "don't" => 2,
                "laugh" => 1,
                "then" => 1,
                "cry" => 1,
                "you're" => 1,
                "getting" => 1,
                "it" => 1,
            },
        ),
        #(
            "with quotations",
            "Joe can't tell between 'large' and large.",
            %{"joe" => 1, "can't" => 1, "tell" => 1, "between" => 1, "large" => 2, "and" => 1},
        ),
        #(
            "substrings from the beginning",
            "Joe can't tell between app, apple and a.",
            %{
                "joe" => 1,
                "can't" => 1,
                "tell" => 1,
                "between" => 1,
                "app" => 1,
                "apple" => 1,
                "and" => 1,
                "a" => 1,
            },
        ),
        #(
            "multiple spaces not detected as a word",
            " multiple   whitespaces",
            %{"multiple" => 1, "whitespaces" => 1},
        ),
        #(
            "alternating word separators not detected as a word",
            ",\n,one,\n ,two \n 'three'",
            %{"one" => 1, "two" => 1, "three" => 1},
        ),
        #(
            "quotation for word with apostrophe",
            "can, can't, 'can't'",
            %{"can" => 1, "can't" => 2},
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, sentence, expected), description {
        assert count_words(sentence) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The whole solution is a four-stage pipeline: lower-case, find the words
  with one regex, and `Iter.frequencies`. The regex
  `[a-z0-9]+('[a-z0-9]+)*` admits an apostrophe only between two letters or
  digits, so quotes around a word fall away without a trimming step.
- Lower-casing happens before matching, so the regex needs no upper-case
  class.
- The expected values are map literals in the table; `Map` equality ignores
  order, so they are written in the canonical order.
- The first "with apostrophes" case (uuid 4185a902) is left out because
  canonical data replaces it with uuid 4ff6c7d7, which is included.
